newsitem.title: FRANCE: Monarch orders four more Airbus craft.
newsitem.headline: Monarch orders four more Airbus craft.

text.p: British holiday carrier Monarch Airlines has ordered four additional Airbus aircraft, consisting of two A330-200 wide-body planes and two A321 narrow-body jets, Airbus said on Monday.

Monarch's A330s will be powered by Rolls Royce Trent 700 engines while the A321s will have International Aero Engines V2533 motors. In a single class layout, the A330s will seat 381 passengers, while the 321s will accommodate 220 passengers.
The catalogue price for A300 models is around $90 million a piece and A321 craft are worth around $54 million, according to industry sources.
The Airbus Industrie consortium comprises French state-owned Aerospatiale, British Aerospace, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
International Aeroengines is a five-firm joint venture led by Britain's Rolls Royce and Pratt and Whitney of U.S. United Technologies Corp.
